metadata.title: Isotopic Evidence for Altitudinal Migration in Late Cretaceous North American Triceratops (HC-2026-042)

abstract: Stable isotope analysis ($\delta^{18}O$ and $\delta^{13}C$) of *Triceratops prorsus* enamel from the Hell Creek Formation (Maastrichtian) provides compelling evidence for seasonal altitudinal migration. Low $\delta^{18}O$ signatures suggest consumption of high-altitude meteoric water, indicating movements between mountainous regions and lowland deltas. This study highlights the underestimated ecological complexity of Late Cretaceous megaherbivores and underscores the utility of micro-sampling techniques for inferring paleo-behavior.
